subject: biology
title: Human Physiology Adventure 1: Digestion and absorption
welcome_lead: Today you'll digest a meal — from mouth to villus.
meta_desc: Biology Human Physiology — digestion, enzymes, absorption, villi, peristalsis.
final_note: You learned digestion hydrolyses polymers via amylase, protease, lipase, and villi maximise SA for absorption of monomers.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Mouth: salivary amylase begins starch digestion (pH 7).

Stomach: HCl creates pH 2; pepsin (a protease) cuts proteins. Mucus protects the lining.

Smooth muscle contractions — peristalsis — propel food.

The duodenum receives:

- Pancreatic juice — amylase, lipase, trypsin, plus HCO₃⁻ to neutralise.
- Bile from liver/gallbladder — emulsifies fats.

The ileum is lined with villi and microvilli — total SA ~250 m². Capillaries take glucose + amino acids; lacteals (lymph) take fatty acids/glycerol as chylomicrons.

Across the villus epithelium:

- Simple diffusion — fatty acids.
- Facilitated diffusion — fructose (GLUT5).
- Active transport — Na⁺-coupled glucose + amino acid uptake (SGLT1).
- Pinocytosis — some peptides.

Oral rehydration therapy exploits Na⁺-glucose cotransport — saved millions of lives from cholera dehydration.

mcqs.q: During an action potential, do Na+ and K+ move through the same channels?
options: Only Na+ moves during an action potential; K+ stays still.
No — voltage-gated Na+ channels open first (depolarisation, Na+ in), then voltage-gated K+ channels open (repolarisation, K+ out).
Sweating removes excess heat by carrying it out as liquid waste.
Na+ and K+ swap places through the same channel at the same time.

sequence.def: Teeth chew; amylase begins starch digestion
Peristalsis pushes the bolus to the stomach
Enzymes finish digestion; nutrients absorbed by villi
Water absorbed from the remaining material
Faeces stored and egested through the anus
